title: Module 10 Challenge: Three Treatments
scenario: Thirty participants with insomnia are randomly assigned to one of three conditions for four weeks: sleep hygiene education only (Group 1), sleep hygiene plus relaxation training (Group 2), or sleep hygiene plus a structured cognitive behavioral program (Group 3). The outcome is hours of additional sleep per week. Each group has 10 people. The means are 10, 12, and 15. SS between = 126.67 and SS within = 270. The analysis gives F(2, 27) = 6.33, p = .006, and eta squared = .32.

parts.q: What does the significant F allow the researchers to conclude?
o: At least one group mean differs from another
The CBT program causes better sleep in every participant
parts.why: The omnibus test does not identify which pairs differ.

parts.q: Why shouldn't the researchers just run three t tests?
o: Each test at .05 inflates the overall Type I error rate to about .14
t tests are not valid for three groups
ANOVA has more power than all t tests
parts.why: 1 minus .95 cubed is about .14. ANOVA with a post hoc test controls it.

parts.q: Write a results paragraph for a journal article. Report F, df, p, and eta squared, interpret the effect size, and say what follow-up analysis is needed before naming the best treatment.
parts.model: A one-way ANOVA showed that the three conditions differed in additional weekly sleep, F(2, 27) = 6.33, p = .006, eta squared = .32. About 32 percent of the variability in additional sleep was associated with condition, which is a large effect. The group means were 10, 12, and 15 hours for sleep hygiene alone, hygiene plus relaxation, and hygiene plus CBT. Because the omnibus F does not reveal which means differ, a post hoc test such as Tukey HSD is needed to compare the pairs, with particular attention to whether the CBT group exceeds the other two. Random assignment supports a causal reading of the group differences, though a sample of 10 per group limits precision.
check: I reported F with both df, p, and eta squared
I interpreted eta squared as a proportion of variability
I said a post hoc test is needed to find which means differ
I did not claim every group differs or every person benefited
